returned_title: European Values Study (EVS) 2017 – Integrated Dataset
justification: Excellent match for the research need. The European Values Study provides harmonized, cross-national survey data on family life, marriage, employment, work values, religion, political attitudes, democracy, national identity, immigration, environmental concerns, gender roles, and interpersonal trust. The 2017 wave includes surveys conducted between 2017 and 2021 across numerous European countries, including Western, Northern, Central, Eastern, and Southeastern Europe. It contains detailed demographic information, including age, gender, education, employment, occupation, income, marital status, and religious affiliation. Particularly suitable for cross-national comparisons and can be combined with earlier EVS waves to examine changes in social values.

returned_title: European Values Study (EVS) Trend File 1981–2017
justification: One of the strongest matches for longitudinal comparative research on European values. This harmonized dataset combines five EVS waves, including the 2008 and 2017 waves, with some fieldwork extending into the early 2020s. It contains more than 224,000 respondents across 49 countries and regions. Topics include work and employment, religion, family and marriage, gender equality, political participation, democracy, national identity, immigration, environmental protection, and social trust. Repeated questions and standardized demographic variables enable comparisons across countries and historical periods. Particularly valuable for identifying long-term changes in cultural, political, and social attitudes across the specified European countries.

returned_title: Joint European Values Study and World Values Survey (EVS/WVS) 2017–2022 Dataset
justification: Exceptionally strong match for the requested subjects, geographical coverage, and period. This integrated dataset harmonizes common questionnaire items from the European Values Study and World Values Survey, covering more than 156,000 respondents across 92 countries and regions worldwide. It includes numerous European countries from the requested list, including Armenia, Czech Republic, Germany, Great Britain, Netherlands, Romania, Russian Federation, Serbia, Slovakia, and Ukraine. Variables address family values, work priorities, religious beliefs, political attitudes, democratic legitimacy, immigration, national identity, environmental protection, gender roles, and social trust. Standardized demographics facilitate cross-national comparisons. The combined dataset is particularly useful for comparing European societies during the late 2010s and early 2020s, although individual countries have different fieldwork years.

returned_title: Integrated Values Surveys (IVS) 1981–2022
justification: Among the most comprehensive resources for the requested research. The Integrated Values Surveys combine the European Values Study and World Values Survey trend files into a harmonized cross-national longitudinal resource. They cover 118 countries and regions, including extensive European coverage, and incorporate observations from the 2010s and early 2020s. Topics closely match all seven requested categories: employment and work values, cultural identity, religion, family relationships, political behavior, gender roles, and environmental attitudes. Additional variables measure democratic preferences, immigration attitudes, institutional confidence, interpersonal trust, and socioeconomic characteristics. Particularly suitable for long-term comparative trend analysis. The integrated file is constructed by merging the separately available EVS and WVS trend datasets using the provided harmonization syntax.

returned_title: World Values Survey (WVS) Wave 7, 2017–2022
justification: Highly relevant cross-national survey dataset measuring social, cultural, economic, religious, and political values during the late 2010s and early 2020s. European participating countries include several from the requested geographical scope. Questions examine employment priorities, family relationships, religious participation, democracy, political trust, national identity, immigration, gender equality, environmental concerns, and interpersonal trust. Detailed demographic variables support comparisons by age, gender, education, income, occupation, and marital status. Particularly useful for comparing contemporary values across European countries and examining changes relative to earlier World Values Survey waves.

returned_title: World Values Survey (WVS) Wave 6, 2010–2014
justification: Important dataset for establishing a baseline of European social and political attitudes during the early 2010s. It contains nationally representative survey observations from participating countries, including several European societies. Topics include labor-market attitudes, family values, religion, national belonging, trust, democratic preferences, political participation, immigration, gender equality, and environmental protection. Detailed respondent demographics support subgroup analysis. Combining Wave 6 with Wave 7 enables comparisons between the early 2010s and late 2010s or early 2020s, subject to country participation and questionnaire comparability.

returned_title: World Values Survey (WVS) Time Series 1981–2022
justification: Strong resource for examining longitudinal changes in attitudes and values across European societies. This harmonized repeated cross-sectional dataset combines seven World Values Survey waves, including Wave 6 from 2010–2014 and Wave 7 from 2017–2022. It measures religion, family relationships, work values, political participation, democratic attitudes, national identity, immigration, gender roles, environmental concerns, and social trust. Demographic information includes age, gender, education, socioeconomic position, employment, and marital status. Particularly useful for identifying changes between the 2010s and 2020s and comparing different European regions. The data follow repeated population samples rather than the same individuals over time.

returned_title: World Values Survey Trend File 1981–2022
justification: Highly relevant harmonized longitudinal survey resource designed to facilitate comparisons of repeated values questions across World Values Survey waves. It includes observations from the 2010s and early 2020s and can be combined with the European Values Study trend file using the common EVS/WVS variable dictionary. Relevant subjects include employment and work orientations, family and marriage, religious beliefs, political participation, democratic values, national identity, immigration, gender equality, environmental attitudes, and interpersonal trust. Particularly useful for constructing harmonized cross-national time series and extending the geographical coverage of European Values Study data.

returned_title: European Social Survey (ESS) – Cumulative Cross-National Survey Data, Multiple Rounds
justification: Excellent complementary dataset for the requested research. The European Social Survey provides repeated cross-sectional surveys across more than 30 European countries, with multiple rounds available throughout the 2010s and 2020s. Its core questionnaire measures social trust, political participation, institutional confidence, immigration attitudes, national identity, religion, social exclusion, subjective well-being, and demographic characteristics. Rotating modules additionally cover democracy, gender, family, climate change, and other social issues. Harmonized questionnaires and extensive methodological documentation enable reliable cross-national trend analysis. The data portal supports customized downloads by survey round, country, and variable. Country coverage varies by round.

returned_title: European Quality of Life Survey (EQLS) – 2011/2012 and 2016 Waves
justification: Relevant complementary dataset for employment, family life, gender roles, social relationships, and institutional trust. Eurofound's European Quality of Life Survey provides comparable cross-national information on employment, household finances, work–life balance, family responsibilities, living conditions, social participation, life satisfaction, and perceived quality of society. The 2011/2012 and 2016 waves are particularly relevant for studying changes during the 2010s. Demographic and socioeconomic variables permit comparisons across European countries and population groups. The survey is especially useful for examining how labor-market conditions and family circumstances relate to social attitudes, although its geographical coverage and emphasis differ from EVS and WVS.

returned_title: International Social Survey Programme (ISSP) – Cross-National Cumulative Datasets
justification: Very strong complementary source covering nearly all requested thematic categories through repeated international survey modules. The ISSP provides harmonized comparative surveys on work orientations, family and changing gender roles, religion, national identity, the role of government, social inequality, and environmental attitudes. Relevant waves include Environment 2010 and 2020, Family and Changing Gender Roles 2012 and 2022, Religion 2018, Role of Government 2016, Social Inequality 2019, and Work Orientations 2015. Topic-specific cumulative datasets facilitate comparisons across multiple decades. Participating European countries overlap substantially with the requested list, although participation varies by module. Standard demographic variables support comparative analysis of social and political attitudes.

returned_title: International Social Survey Programme (ISSP) 2022 – Family and Changing Gender Roles V
justification: Highly relevant for the family life, marriage, employment, and gender-role components of the research need. This international survey examines attitudes toward marriage, family arrangements, childcare, women's employment, household responsibilities, gender equality, and the division of paid and unpaid work. It provides harmonized observations from participating countries, including European societies, together with demographic and socioeconomic characteristics. Particularly useful for studying gender norms and family values during the early 2020s and comparing results with earlier ISSP family modules, especially 2012. Country coverage must be checked because not all requested countries participate, and the Great Britain data are provided separately from the integrated file.

returned_title: International Social Survey Programme (ISSP) – Environment 1993, 2000, 2010 and 2020
justification: Especially relevant for longitudinal analysis of environmental attitudes and conservation values. The ISSP Environment modules provide repeated cross-national measurements of environmental concern, willingness to make economic sacrifices for environmental protection, environmental behavior, trust in institutions, and perceptions of environmental risks. The 2010 and 2020 waves closely match the requested time period and allow comparisons of changing environmental values across participating European countries. Harmonized demographic variables support analysis by age, gender, education, employment, income, and other socioeconomic characteristics. The cumulative dataset facilitates comparisons across multiple survey waves.

returned_title: International Social Survey Programme (ISSP) – National Identity 1995, 2003 and 2013
justification: Strong thematic match for cultural and national identity, immigration, citizenship, and social belonging. The ISSP National Identity modules examine national pride, criteria for belonging to a nation, attitudes toward immigrants, cultural diversity, international integration, and perceptions of national institutions. The 2013 wave provides observations within the requested decade, while earlier waves support longitudinal comparisons. The cumulative resource harmonizes repeated variables across participating countries. Detailed demographic information enables investigation of differences in national identity and immigration attitudes by generation, education, employment, gender, and socioeconomic status.

returned_title: International Social Survey Programme (ISSP) – Religion 1991, 1998, 2008 and 2018
justification: Highly relevant for examining religious values, secularization, social trust, and connections between religious beliefs and political or family attitudes. The ISSP Religion modules measure religious identification, religious attendance, beliefs, religious upbringing, attitudes toward religious institutions, and related social values. The 2018 wave provides observations within the requested period, while the cumulative dataset enables comparison with earlier surveys. The data include participating European countries and standardized demographic information, making them valuable for investigating differences in religiosity across generations, socioeconomic groups, and national contexts.

returned_title: International Social Survey Programme (ISSP) – Work Orientations 1989, 1997, 2005 and 2015
justification: Directly relevant to labor and employment attitudes across European societies. The ISSP Work Orientations modules examine job satisfaction, employment preferences, job security, work motivation, working conditions, career opportunities, and the importance of work relative to other aspects of life. The 2015 wave provides a relevant observation point during the 2010s, while earlier waves support trend analysis. Harmonized demographic information allows comparisons by gender, age, education, occupation, employment status, and socioeconomic position. Particularly useful for connecting employment attitudes with family responsibilities, gender roles, and broader cultural values.

returned_title: International Social Survey Programme (ISSP) – Role of Government 1985, 1990, 1996, 2006 and 2016
justification: Relevant to political behavior and attitudes, institutional trust, and preferences concerning government responsibilities. The ISSP Role of Government modules examine public expectations of government, redistribution, welfare policies, economic intervention, civil liberties, and the balance between state and individual responsibility. The 2016 wave provides observations during the requested period, while cumulative data support comparisons across earlier decades. Participating European countries and standardized socioeconomic variables make the dataset useful for examining how political values differ by country, generation, education, employment status, and social class.

returned_title: International Social Survey Programme (ISSP) – Social Inequality 1987, 1992, 1999, 2009 and 2019
justification: Useful complementary dataset for examining employment, gender, political attitudes, social inequality, and perceptions of fairness across European countries. The 2019 module measures beliefs about income inequality, social mobility, economic opportunity, distributive justice, and the legitimacy of socioeconomic differences. Earlier waves provide a longitudinal perspective on changing attitudes toward inequality. Demographic variables permit comparisons by gender, age, education, occupation, employment, and socioeconomic status. Particularly valuable for exploring relationships between economic circumstances, political preferences, and broader social values.

returned_title: European Values Study (EVS) 2017 – Integrated Dataset and Matrix Design Data
justification: Important supplementary resource for maximizing geographical coverage and questionnaire completeness within the fifth European Values Study wave. The full EVS 2017 release includes the principal integrated dataset and a separate matrix-design dataset containing approximately 10,500 respondents from Germany, Iceland, Switzerland, and the Netherlands. These countries are included in the requested geographical scope. The surveys address family relationships, work, religion, national identity, politics, trust, immigration, gender roles, and environmental values. The matrix-design data are especially important when analyzing questions that are not fully represented in the main integrated file. Researchers should consult the documentation before combining the two datasets.

returned_title: European Values Study (EVS) 1981–2017 – Restricted-Use Longitudinal Dataset
justification: Specialized extension of the European Values Study trend dataset for research requiring more detailed demographic and geographical information. The restricted-use file supplements the public EVS longitudinal data with sensitive variables, including detailed occupational classifications and selected subnational geographical identifiers. It is particularly relevant for studying how employment characteristics, local contexts, and socioeconomic conditions relate to family values, religion, national identity, political attitudes, gender roles, and environmental concerns. It covers multiple EVS waves, including observations relevant to the 2010s and early 2020s. Access requires additional authorization and compliance with data protection conditions.

returned_title: European Values Study and World Values Survey – Joint 2017–2022 Dataset, WVS Archive Edition
justification: Official World Values Survey archive edition of the harmonized EVS/WVS 2017–2022 dataset. It provides the same integrated comparative survey resource as the GESIS edition, offering an alternative official access route. The dataset contains common questions on family, work, religion, politics, democracy, immigration, national identity, environmental values, gender equality, and social trust. It includes surveys from numerous European countries and detailed demographic variables. Particularly appropriate for constructing comparative European analyses during the late 2010s and early 2020s. This is an alternative distribution of the joint dataset rather than an independent additional survey.

returned_title: Politbarometer 2025 (Cumulated Data Set) – Forschungsgruppe Wahlen / ZDF
justification: Excellent match and the strongest single dataset for this research need. The Politbarometer 2025 (GESIS ZA9151) contains representative German public opinion surveys conducted throughout 2025. It covers voting intentions and party preferences for the 2025 federal election, evaluations of potential governing coalitions, preferred chancellor, assessments of Olaf Scholz, Friedrich Merz, Robert Habeck and Alice Weidel, party popularity, government satisfaction, and political competence. Additional questions address migration and asylum, economic conditions, pensions, climate and energy policies, defense and military spending, Russia's war against Ukraine, the European Union, democratic satisfaction, and political institutions. Respondent characteristics support demographic analysis. Its repeated surveys make it particularly valuable for examining changes in public opinion before and after the February 2025 federal election.

returned_title: GLES Cross-Section 2025, Post-Election – German Longitudinal Election Study
justification: Highly relevant representative individual-level survey conducted after Germany's federal election on February 23, 2025. GESIS study ZA10100 surveyed 7,336 respondents between February 24 and April 23, 2025, using online and paper questionnaires. The dataset provides detailed information on electoral participation, voting decisions, party identification, political preferences, evaluations of political parties and candidates, and political attitudes. It is particularly useful for studying the relationship between electoral choices, political opinions, and respondent demographics. Its standardized election-study design also supports comparisons with previous German federal elections.

returned_title: GLES Rolling Cross-Section 2025 – German Longitudinal Election Study
justification: Very strong match for investigating public opinion and electoral behavior surrounding the 2025 federal election. The survey collected observations during the pre-election period from January 6 to February 22, 2025, and the post-election period from February 25 to March 31, 2025. Its rolling cross-sectional design enables researchers to investigate changes in party preferences, campaign evaluations, political attitudes, candidate perceptions, and voting intentions as the election approached. Particularly useful for analyzing the effects of political developments and campaign events on voter attitudes, with individual-level demographic information.

returned_title: GLES Tracking 2009–2026, Cumulation – German Longitudinal Election Study
justification: Highly relevant longitudinal collection of repeated German political opinion surveys, including observations from the 2025 federal election period. GESIS study ZA6832 combines tracking surveys collected between 2009 and March 2026. It supports analysis of trends in voting intentions, political party preferences, political attitudes, electoral behavior, and evaluations of political actors. Particularly valuable for distinguishing election-specific changes in public opinion from longer-term trends and for comparing political attitudes during the Scholz and Merz government periods. Individual-level survey responses allow analysis across demographic groups.

returned_title: GLES Tracking February 2025, T60 – German Longitudinal Election Study
justification: Directly relevant survey conducted February 12–20, 2025, immediately before the federal election. This GLES tracking wave provides a focused snapshot of German voters' political preferences and attitudes during the final campaign period. It is useful for examining party support, candidate evaluations, political issue priorities, and electoral expectations before voting took place. Its timing makes it especially suitable for comparison with post-election surveys and for identifying differences in electoral attitudes across demographic groups.

returned_title: GLES Tracking March 2025, T60W – Post-Election Survey and Data Donation
justification: Relevant post-election component of the German Longitudinal Election Study, identified as GESIS ZA10132. Conducted March 5–21, 2025, it provides information collected shortly after the federal election and during the early government-formation period. It is particularly useful for investigating changes in electoral attitudes, reactions to election outcomes, and political preferences following the vote. The accompanying data-donation component offers additional opportunities for studying political information behavior. The linked official GLES landing page identifies the study and provides access to its documentation and data release.

returned_title: GLES Tracking May 2025, T61 – German Longitudinal Election Study
justification: Relevant post-election public opinion survey conducted May 14–23, 2025, following the formation of Germany's new federal government. It provides an opportunity to examine political preferences and evaluations in the transition from the election campaign to the new government. Particularly useful alongside the February and March 2025 GLES waves for assessing changes in party support, political attitudes, and perceptions of political leadership. The study forms part of the established GLES tracking infrastructure and supports demographic comparisons.

returned_title: Politbarometer 2024 (Cumulated Data Set) – Forschungsgruppe Wahlen / ZDF
justification: Important complementary dataset providing the political opinion baseline immediately preceding the 2025 federal election. The dataset includes repeated representative surveys conducted throughout 2024, covering voting intentions, party preferences, coalition preferences, assessments of the Scholz government, party and politician evaluations, and perceived party competence. It also contains questions on migration, economic conditions, pensions, energy and climate policy, democracy, and other political issues. Particularly useful for comparing public opinion before and after the collapse of the governing coalition and the subsequent federal election. Respondent demographics support subgroup comparisons.

returned_title: ARD-DeutschlandTrend – German Public Opinion Survey Series
justification: Highly relevant collection of German public opinion surveys conducted by infratest dimap for ARD. DeutschlandTrend surveys examine federal voting intentions, party preferences, satisfaction with the chancellor and federal government, political leadership evaluations, and the perceived competence of political parties. Survey questions also address economic conditions, immigration and asylum, pensions, social policy, democratic satisfaction, European integration, and major political developments. The GESIS collection provides access to archived research datasets, making it a useful complementary source to Politbarometer and GLES. Coverage and availability of individual 2025 survey waves should be checked in the linked catalogue.

returned_title: Politbarometer 1977–2024 (Partial Cumulation) – Long-Term German Political Opinion Trends
justification: Useful supplementary dataset for placing German political attitudes surrounding the 2025 election into historical perspective. GESIS study ZA2391 combines 74 selected time series from Politbarometer surveys conducted between 1977 and 2024. It supports longitudinal analysis of electoral preferences, political leadership evaluations, government satisfaction, and other recurring indicators of political opinion. Although it does not include the 2025 election itself, it can be combined analytically with the 2025 Politbarometer dataset to distinguish recent political changes from established patterns of public opinion.

returned_title: Germany Monitor 2025 – Regional In-depth Survey (Deutschland-Monitor '25)
justification: Relevant complementary public opinion dataset covering political and social attitudes in Germany during 2025. GESIS study ZA9149 contains responses from 4,018 individuals surveyed between July 23 and September 12, 2025. The study examines public attitudes toward political and societal change, including migration, economic and social developments, perceptions of Germany's future, and political institutions. Its regional design makes it especially useful for investigating geographical differences in political attitudes and public perceptions after the federal election. The dataset includes individual-level survey information and demographic characteristics. It is less election-specific than Politbarometer or GLES but adds valuable contextual measures.

returned_title: GLES Panel 2025 – German Longitudinal Election Study
justification: Highly relevant longitudinal survey program following German voters across multiple waves around the 2025 federal election. Unlike repeated cross-sectional surveys, the GLES Panel allows researchers to examine how political preferences and attitudes change within the same individuals over time. Its research focus includes electoral choices, party attachments, political evaluations, and political behavior. The panel is especially valuable for investigating whether changing opinions about government performance, economic concerns, migration, and political leadership correspond to changes in voting preferences. Respondent characteristics facilitate analysis of demographic differences in political attitude change. The official landing page lists the 2025 panel studies and their data releases.

returned_title: ALLBUS – German General Social Survey, Political Attitudes and Democracy
justification: Relevant supplementary survey collection for examining broader political attitudes and democratic orientations among the German population. ALLBUS datasets include measures of party identification, voting intentions, political ideology, satisfaction with democracy, confidence in institutions, political participation, immigration attitudes, social policy preferences, environmental protection, and defense spending. They also provide extensive demographic and socioeconomic information. Although ALLBUS is not specifically designed around the 2025 federal election, available 2020s waves provide useful background variables and historical comparisons for interpreting election-specific survey findings.

returned_title: German Longitudinal Environmental Study (GLEN) – Release 1.0 (2024–2026), GESIS Study ZA9085
justification: Excellent match and the most directly relevant dataset for the research need. GLEN is a Germany-wide longitudinal environmental panel launched in 2024 that collects repeated self-administered survey data on environmental attitudes, environmentally relevant behavior, climate change, sustainability, and public acceptance of environmental policy measures. It also addresses environmental inequality, distributive justice, political attitudes, consumption, mobility, media use, leisure activities, life satisfaction, and sociodemographic characteristics. The first release, published in 2026, contains five surveys conducted between November 2024 and January 2026, covering more than 25,000 participants. The study uses predominantly online self-administered surveys, with a broader mixed-mode recruitment design. Its longitudinal structure supports analysis of changes in environmental attitudes, behavior, and policy acceptance over time. The dataset is archived by GESIS and available for scientific research.

returned_title: German Longitudinal Environmental Study (GLEN) – Official Study Portal
justification: Official landing page for the German Longitudinal Environmental Study, a nationwide panel examining environmental and climate-related attitudes and behaviors. The study repeatedly surveys adults across Germany to investigate changes in environmental awareness, sustainability practices, and attitudes toward climate policies. It is designed to support research on environmental inequalities, environmental conditions in residential areas, social influences, and the distributional consequences of environmental protection measures. GLEN began in 2024 and is planned as a long-term research infrastructure extending through 2035, making it particularly relevant for research spanning 2024–2026 and subsequent years. The portal provides information about the study, participating research institutions, survey activities, and access to GESIS data releases.

returned_title: Environmental Consciousness in Germany 2024 (Umweltbewusstsein in Deutschland 2024)
justification: Highly relevant complementary dataset examining environmental awareness, environmental attitudes, environmental behavior, and perceptions of environmental policy among Germany's population. The 2024 survey investigates relationships between environmental conditions, health, quality of life, willingness to adopt sustainable behaviors, and support for environmental protection measures. It includes sociodemographic and sociocultural information useful for studying environmental inequality and differences in attitudes between population groups. The survey forms part of a repeated national study series conducted since 1996, enabling comparisons across survey years. However, unlike GLEN, it is primarily a repeated cross-sectional survey rather than a panel following the same individuals. It is therefore particularly useful for contextualizing longitudinal GLEN findings.

returned_title: GESIS Panel.pop – Population Sample, Standard Edition
justification: Relevant supplementary longitudinal panel dataset covering Germany's adult population. The GESIS Panel.pop uses a probability-based mixed-mode design in which participants complete self-administered questionnaires online or on paper. Its repeated survey waves allow researchers to examine changes in social attitudes, political preferences, consumption, values, and other aspects of social behavior. Depending on the modules included in particular waves, environmental and sustainability-related variables may also be available. The panel is particularly useful for studying relationships between environmental attitudes and broader social, demographic, psychological, and political characteristics. It matches the requested longitudinal and mixed-mode methodology, although environmental policy acceptance and environmental inequality are not its exclusive research focus. Availability of individual 2024–2026 waves should be checked in the release documentation.

returned_title: Environmental Awareness Study 2026 (Umweltbewusstseinsstudie 2026)
justification: Highly relevant ongoing national survey project examining environmental awareness, environmentally relevant behavior, and perceptions of environmental and climate policy in Germany. The 2026 study continues a long-running research series and adds particular emphasis on circular economy practices and gender equality. Approximately 2,000 respondents are included in the representative core survey, supplemented by qualitative research and a separate youth survey. Its social and demographic measures are relevant for investigating environmental inequality, sustainability attitudes, and differences in environmental policy acceptance across population groups. Data collection was scheduled for spring and summer 2026, with principal findings expected in winter 2026–2027. As of November 2026, this is a study landing page rather than confirmation of a publicly released microdataset. It offers strong thematic relevance but does not provide the same individual-level longitudinal panel structure as GLEN.

returned_title: Environmental Awareness in Germany – Long-Term Time Series and Integrated Dataset
justification: Relevant resource for historical and contemporary comparisons of environmental attitudes and behavior in Germany. The Federal Environment Agency's 2024 Environmental Awareness Study provides access to information about the study and links to integrated longitudinal time-series resources. These resources support the examination of trends in environmental concern, climate awareness, sustainable consumption, perceived environmental risks, and public attitudes toward environmental protection policies. The 2024 study also addresses environmental health inequalities, socioeconomic differences, and environmental justice. Its historical coverage makes it particularly valuable for interpreting changes observed in the GLEN panel during 2024–2026. The underlying surveys are repeated cross-sections, however, rather than repeated observations of the same individuals.

returned_title: Environmental Awareness in Germany 2024 – Federal Environment Agency Data Cube
justification: Official data portal providing structured statistical information from Germany's Environmental Awareness Study series. It supports analysis of environmental attitudes, climate concerns, household consumption, environmental health, and the relationship between environmental protection and economic or social conditions. The underlying study series has been conducted approximately every two years since 1996, allowing researchers to compare environmental awareness across different periods, including 2024. The portal is useful for obtaining contextual indicators and examining broader national trends alongside GLEN's individual-level longitudinal panel data. It is particularly relevant to environmental attitudes, sustainability, consumption behavior, and social indicators, although it is not a substitute for respondent-level panel microdata.

returned_title: Relevance of Environmental Protection in Society – U-INDEX Survey Data 2024–2025
justification: Relevant complementary dataset containing survey information on public attitudes toward environmental protection collected in Germany during 2024 and 2025. The dataset includes an Excel data file covering these survey years and can support analyses of the perceived importance of environmental protection and changes in environmental awareness. Its observation period closely overlaps with the requested 2024–2026 timeframe. It may be useful for comparing public environmental priorities with GLEN findings or exploring whether environmental concerns remain salient across survey periods. However, its suitability for individual-level longitudinal analysis, mixed-mode comparisons, and detailed environmental inequality research requires examination of the accompanying documentation.

returned_title: GESIS Panel / GESIS Panel.pop – Population Sample (2014–Present)
justification: Excellent match for the research need. The GESIS Panel is a probability-based, longitudinal, mixed-mode survey of the adult German-speaking population in Germany. Regular bi-monthly survey waves began in 2014, following recruitment in 2013. The panel includes refreshment cohorts recruited in 2016, 2018, 2021, and 2023. It covers political attitudes and behaviour, elections, government, media consumption, information technology, social conditions, economic attitudes, inequality, psychology, health, employment, family life, environmental attitudes, and numerous other social science topics. The panel provides harmonized demographic information, survey participation modes, and sampling weights, enabling longitudinal and cross-sectional analyses. This is the strongest overall match.

returned_title: GESIS Panel.pop – Scientific Use File, Standard Edition, and Extended Edition
justification: Direct access point for the longitudinal GESIS Panel datasets. The available editions provide repeated observations from probability-sampled adults in Germany, covering the 2010s and 2020s. They are particularly suitable for research requiring harmonized demographic variables, including education, income, marital status, and other socioeconomic characteristics, together with survey participation information and weighting variables. The longitudinal structure supports analyses of changes in political behaviour, economic conditions, health, psychological well-being, social inequality, employment, media use, technology adoption, and environmental attitudes. Different data editions have different access requirements.

returned_title: GESIS Panel.pop – Special Survey on the Coronavirus SARS-CoV-2 Outbreak in Germany (2020)
justification: Highly relevant COVID-19 survey linked to the GESIS Panel longitudinal infrastructure. The special survey was conducted from March 17 to March 29, 2020, among a subsample of online panel participants. It provides information about the pandemic and its social, psychological, behavioural, and political implications. Its connection to the probability-based GESIS Panel makes it especially useful for examining pandemic experiences alongside pre-pandemic demographic information and longitudinal survey responses. The GESIS data-access page includes the COVID-19 Public Use File.

returned_title: GESIS Panel – Longitudinal Core Studies and Survey Documentation
justification: Official documentation and access point for the GESIS Panel longitudinal core studies. These repeatedly measure important characteristics beyond basic demographics, including personality, psychological traits, human values, political behaviour, subjective well-being, quality of life, environmental attitudes, media consumption, and information and communication technology use. The documentation is valuable for identifying comparable variables across bi-monthly waves, examining questionnaire changes, and understanding demographic harmonization. It also provides information necessary for longitudinal research designs and appropriate interpretation of panel data.

returned_title: GESIS Panel.pop – Sample and Recruitment Documentation
justification: Essential supporting resource for researchers requiring probability-based longitudinal data with refreshment cohorts. It documents the original recruitment of approximately 4,900 panel members in 2013–2014 and subsequent probability-based refreshment samples in 2016, 2018, 2021, and 2023. It describes recruitment procedures, target populations, and the mixed-mode design that accommodates online and paper questionnaire participation. Particularly useful for assessing sample representativeness, cohort comparability, selection mechanisms, and longitudinal attrition.

returned_title: GESIS Panel – Standard Edition Dataset
justification: Dataset discovery record for the GESIS Panel Standard Edition. This is a strong match for interdisciplinary research combining political attitudes, social stratification, economic conditions, psychological characteristics, media use, information technology, and demographic indicators. Documented variables include internet usage frequency, social media participation, technology adoption, communication devices, and attitudes toward technological developments. The dataset's repeated-wave structure supports analyses of changes in individual behaviour and attitudes, while its connection to the broader GESIS Panel provides access to demographic and methodological documentation.

returned_title: GESIS Panel – Probability-Based Mixed-Mode Panel Dataset and Wave Documentation
justification: Detailed GESIS archival documentation describing the probability-based panel design, bi-monthly data collection, refreshment cohorts, longitudinal core modules, and weighting procedures. The original cohort entered regular survey participation in early 2014, with additional respondents recruited subsequently to compensate for attrition. The documentation explicitly discusses integration weights for combining cohorts and identifies recurring measures of political orientations, personality, well-being, environmental behaviour, and information technology use. Especially relevant for researchers seeking defensible longitudinal analyses with appropriate demographic adjustments and survey weights.

returned_title: German Internet Panel (GIP) – University of Mannheim (2012–Present)
justification: Closely related alternative probability-based longitudinal survey of people living in private households in Germany. The German Internet Panel began in 2012, recruited refreshment samples in 2014 and 2018, and conducts online questionnaires approximately every two months. It covers political and economic decision-making, government policies, elections, welfare attitudes, inequality, education, employment, health, and socioeconomic characteristics. The panel provides extensive longitudinal data and demographic information, making it highly relevant for research spanning the 2010s and 2020s. Unlike the GESIS Panel, it is primarily an online survey rather than a mixed-mode online and paper panel.

returned_title: German Internet Panel (GIP) – Scientific Use Files and Data Access
justification: Official University of Mannheim access point for German Internet Panel scientific-use datasets distributed through the GESIS Data Archive. The survey provides repeated individual observations across multiple years, with questionnaires administered every two months. Research topics include political attitudes, economic policy, public expenditure, social inequality, health, employment, education, and demographic characteristics. The longitudinal survey design and refreshment cohorts support analyses of individual-level change over time. This is a useful complementary dataset to the GESIS Panel, although its recruitment history and survey modes differ.

returned_title: German Internet Panel (GIP) – Questionnaires and Documentation
justification: Official documentation for identifying and comparing variables across German Internet Panel survey waves. The panel administers questionnaires every other month, with an annual September core wave that updates important socioeconomic and demographic characteristics. This makes the documentation particularly useful for identifying repeated measures of education, income, family circumstances, employment, political attitudes, and social behaviour. It also provides access to questionnaire information from the Mannheim Corona Study, facilitating research on COVID-19 and its relationship to longer-term social and economic outcomes.

returned_title: GESIS Panel.pop – Overview, Sampling Framework, and Refreshment Cohorts
justification: Official description of the GESIS Panel population sample and its longitudinal design. The panel initially recruited German-speaking adults aged 18–70 and began regular survey waves in 2014. Refreshment samples were subsequently introduced in 2016, 2018, 2021, and 2023, with adult respondents aged 18 and older eligible for the refreshment cohorts. The resource clarifies the distinction between the probability-based GESIS Panel.pop and the newer GESIS Panel.dbd infrastructure. This distinction is important because the research need specifically calls for probability sampling, repeated bi-monthly measurements, and integration of multiple recruitment cohorts.

returned_title: GESIS Panel – Longitudinal Psychological Research on the COVID-19 Outbreak in Germany
justification: Foundational methodological publication describing the establishment of the GESIS Panel as an open, probability-based, mixed-mode longitudinal panel of the German population. Although this DOI identifies a methodological article rather than a downloadable dataset, it provides valuable context for evaluating the panel's sampling design, population coverage, survey modes, and suitability for repeated-measures research. The associated GESIS Panel infrastructure includes longitudinal psychological and social indicators as well as COVID-19-related survey modules. Researchers should use the GESIS Panel data-access pages to obtain the actual datasets.

returned_title: News on TikTok: An Annotated Dataset of TikTok Videos from German-Speaking News Outlets in 2023 (Version 2.0.0)
justification: Exact match for the research need. Published by GESIS in 2025, this open-access dataset contains 8,623 TikTok videos published in 2023 by 18 major German-speaking news outlets across Germany, Austria, and Switzerland. It combines TikTok metadata with human-coded annotations covering 25 variables, including visual presentation styles, text overlays, audio elements, interactive features, journalistic content characteristics, and news values derived from journalism theory. Videos were collected using the TikTok Research API in January 2024 and manually annotated between September 2024 and February 2025. The dataset supports comparative journalism research, multimodal content analysis, news value theory, and the development of automated annotation methods. This is the most comprehensive and directly relevant dataset identified.

returned_title: News on TikTok: An Annotated Dataset of TikTok Videos from German-Speaking News Outlets in 2023 (Version 1.0.0)
justification: Exact match for the requested research characteristics. This earlier version contains more than 4,000 human-coded TikTok videos published during 2023 by major news organizations in Germany, Austria, and Switzerland. The sample includes every second video published by selected news outlets during the study period. Annotations include visual style, text overlays, audio presence, and journalism-related news values. Data collection occurred in January 2024, followed by manual coding from September through December 2024. Particularly suitable for research requiring a systematically selected, manually annotated sample of German-language news videos. Researchers seeking the complete collection should use Version 2.0.0 instead.
